coal.trend_notes: Coal output fell 5.8% year-on-year in April 2026. Structural headwinds from global energy transition, ESG-driven capital withdrawal, and reduced Eskom demand as renewables scale. Richards Bay Coal Terminal export market active but under price and volume pressure. Waterberg coalfields (Limpopo) remain a long-term strategic reserve with slower development. Domestic power generation remains the stabilising demand floor.

chrome.trend_notes: Chromium production +37.3% in January 2026; +3.9% for full year 2025. South Africa holds world's largest chrome reserves. Demand driven by robust global stainless steel demand from post-pandemic manufacturing recovery (China, India). Battery electric vehicle and green energy applications creating emerging demand. Steelpoort valley and Bushveld Complex in strong growth mode.

iron_ore.trend_notes: Iron ore production decreased 1.9% in 2026, linked to reduced Chinese steel output (down 4% in 2025). However, Kumba Iron Ore (Anglo American) executing R11.2bn Sishen Ultra-High Dense Media Separation (UHD-MS) project â€” increasing premium proportion from 18% to 55% of output. Construction commenced November 2024; initial operations expected 2026. Capital upgrade creates significant equipment demand even as total volumes are under pressure.

Sibanye-Stillwater active in equipment and services procurement (loading and hauling RFI confirmed June 2026). Valterra Platinum (fmr. Amplats) using SAP Ariba for supplier procurement.

gold.trend_notes: Gold sales +12.2% to R19.5bn underpinned by record gold prices (above $3,000/oz in 2026). Qala Shallows Gold Mine (West Wits Mining, Witwatersrand) opened late 2025 â€” first new underground gold mine in SA in 15 years. Targeting 70,000oz/year. Phase of larger Witwatersrand Basin Project. High gold price incentivising marginal mine re-openings and junior miner development.
